note: MasonryZap parameters in human units only: percents and plain addresses. No bps, no wei — deploy code converts (0.5 percent becomes 50 in the contract's routeFeeBps).

zap._feeRecipient: Wallet that receives the route fee — the DAO/Treasury wallet the other protocol fees route to (fees are always wallets in this protocol, never the Treasury contract). Set with setFeeRecipient after deployment.
zap._maxSpotTwapDivergencePercent: Spot-vs-TWAP manipulation guard: before any swap, a route compares the pool's live spot price against its TWAP (read from the pool hook's own oracle — V4 pools keep no price history, the hook's recorded observations are the price history). If spot has moved away from the TWAP by more than this percent, the route refuses (SpotTwapDivergence) — a price pushed earlier in the block is never priced in as if it were real. Worked example: at 2 percent with xTOMB's TWAP at $1.00, a zap refuses while spot sits above $1.02 or below $0.98, and executes normally at $1.015. PROVISIONAL DEFAULT (Bingo, 2026-11-09, flagged for Jess — not his number): 2 percent. On-chain safety bound: the contract rejects any setting above 5 percent — that hard cap is code, not config (it mirrors the tolerance ceiling MasonryBuybackGuard sets for its own guard). Applied with setTwapGuard after deployment; the contract's built-in default equals this value.
zap._routeFeePercent: The one house toll (spec section 15): percent of the input taken once, before conversion, to the fee recipient — charged in the input asset on every route including swap(). 0.5 = one half of one percent. Worked example: zapping 1,000 USDC into a farm pool pays exactly 5 USDC of route fee and works the remaining 995 into the position. The Genesis LP route is EXEMPT — it always pays 0 here, because staking those shares into Genesis pool 1 charges the 0.5% Genesis LP deposit burn fee instead; one action never pays the toll twice. The Genesis standard route DOES pay it: pool 0 deposits are credited gross (no deposit fee exists there), so there is nothing to double. On-chain safety bound: the contract rejects any setting above 5 percent.
zap._routes: zap(inputToken, amountIn, destination, minOutput, deadline) is the generic entry; named wrappers: zapToGenesisLP, zapToFarmLevel, zapToFarmShare, zapToMasonry, zapToGenesisStandard, zapAssetToGenesisStandard. Every staking route ends STAKED for the caller (LP created and staked, or the share/standard token staked in the Boardroom / Genesis pool 0). swap(inputToken, amountIn, outputToken, minOut, deadline) is the engine's token-to-token route — the surface the frontend Swap page consumes (stable<->asset on each hooked pool, asset<->asset bridged through the stable). Accepted zap inputs: the stable for every route, plus each destination's own stake asset directly (vault shares into the LP routes, the standard asset into Genesis pool 0, xSHARE into the Masonry).
zap._twapWindowMinutes: The TWAP window the guard averages over, in minutes: the oracle reports the mean price across this span of recorded history, and spot must sit within maxSpotTwapDivergencePercent of THAT mean. Worked example: at 30 minutes, a price that spiked 2 minutes ago barely moves the average, so spot-vs-TWAP shows nearly the whole spike as divergence and the zap refuses; a price that has traded at its new level for the full 30 minutes has a TWAP that agrees with spot and zaps flow. On-chain bounds, enforced in code: minimum 5 minutes (one oracle observation bucket — a shorter average is not resolvable from the recorded history), maximum 60 minutes (the oracle's lookback). Applied with setTwapGuard after deployment; the contract's built-in default equals this value. WARM-UP CONSEQUENCE — read before launch: the guard fails closed. After a pool opens, and after any quiet stretch longer than the oracle's freshness limit, swapping routes refuse with TwapNotReady until the configured window has filled with real trading history — the warm-up lasts one full window (30 minutes at the default) after pool creation. Per the launch ruling this warm-up is WAITED OUT, never seeded away: there is no oracle seeding, farms simply start paying one full TWAP window after their pool is created. The guard applies only to routes that execute a swap; direct-stake routes (standard Genesis, staking an asset already held) never consult it and are open from minute one.
zap._wiring: Deploy order: staking stack first (MasonryGenesisStaking, ShareRewardPool with pid 0 = Level vault and pid 1 = Square vault, Boardroom initialized with the Square token as its share), then the zap against them. AFTER deploying the zap, wire it as the beneficiary-staking operator on all three surfaces or every zap-and-stake reverts: MasonryGenesisStaking.setZapOperator(zap) by the Genesis schedule's scheduler, ShareRewardPool.setZapOperator(zap) by the farm operator, Boardroom.setZapOperator(zap) by the Boardroom operator. If the TWAP guard settings in this file differ from the built-in defaults, apply them with setTwapGuard after deployment (percent and minutes here convert to the contract's units: 2 percent = 200, 30 minutes = 1800 seconds). The Genesis standard pool's stake asset is read from the staking contract at deploy time (its constructor forbids the reward token there) — the zap supports the stable, xTOMB or xSHARE as that asset and reverts at construction for anything it cannot price.
